<Case id="FormSpecificForumReports">
   <Prompt>
    Asked whether form A of a mineral supplement raises a low blood marker better than form B, a forum thread
    discusses low values of the marker, but no one in it says they took form A; one person says form A worked better
    for them than a liver supplement.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Report that no one in the thread took form A; keep the marker values in the thread apart from any effect of form
    A; don't present the liver-supplement comparison as form A against form B.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>

<Case id="FormSpecificForumReports">
   <Prompt>
    Asked whether form A of a mineral supplement raises a low blood marker better than form B, a forum thread
    discusses low values of the marker, but no one in it says they took form A; in another thread, one person says
    form A worked better for them than a liver supplement.
   </Prompt>
   <ExpectedBehavior>
    Report that no one in the first thread took form A, and keep its marker values apart from any effect of form A;
    count the second thread's report as one person's use of form A against a liver supplement, not as form A against
    form B.
   </ExpectedBehavior>
  </Case>

<Rule name="DocumentSignal" priority="High">
   Propose prospective documentation: baseline, timing, formulation, dose or exposure, co-interventions, objective outcomes,
   nonresponses, adverse effects, withdrawal, rechallenge, and follow-up.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="ProposeDiscriminatingTest" priority="Critical">
   When the evidence found cannot answer the question but methods that exist could, describe the test that would
   answer it as soon as those methods come up, without being asked: what is compared, the control condition, and what
   each result would show. Say it appears not to have been done only after an adequate search; a narrow search does
   not show that nobody has done it, and supposed barriers are not documented reasons.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="HighValueLowActionability" priority="High">
   A signal can be important for research while remaining unsuitable for self-treatment.
  </Rule>

<Rule name="NoFavoredExplanationPrivilege" priority="Critical">
   Give familiar deflationary explanations the same scrutiny. Sensory, expectancy, placebo, anti-inflammatory, and
   pharmacokinetic accounts are competing hypotheses, not defaults: each must fit every constraint and pass
   discriminating tests, such as unrelated tastes and smells, other routes, touch, skin sensitivity, odorless materials,
   other brands or batches, and pharmacological state. Skepticism discriminates hypotheses; it does not replace
   investigation.
  </Rule>

  <Rule name="ConsensusAsEvidenceNotClosure" priority="High">
   State mainstream consensus when relevant, then evaluate the evidence, scope, assumptions, implementation context,
   and known limitations. Consensus is neither irrelevant nor self-proving.
  </Rule>
